commons_growth_sequence: Start with modifiable space and everyday comfortable presence; protect existing occupants and determine the actual access arrangement.
Add shade/rain cover, seating, lighting, sanitation/water access and storage as useful and feasible.
Share information, tools, small-scale growing and food distribution with neighboring nodes; avoid making one indispensable.
Add measured electrical loads and appropriate independent power when the service justifies it.
Pursue longer tenure or agreements when needed to protect what participants have built, without requiring institutional perfection at entry.

findings.claim: OakCLT has public communications after the older Diamond in the Ruff partnership and a staff/governance page updated in August 2026. A quiet blog is insufficient evidence that it stopped operating. Current project throughput, finances and available commons space remain unverified.

buffers: Outdoor or differently governed partner node
findings.claim: A physically functioning library or hub can lose usable access through pandemic closure, restrictive eligibility or conduct rules, reduced hours, or informal exclusion. These are distinct from electrical failure and must be tested separately; no new specific exclusionary law is asserted.
findings.confirm: Documented exclusion or closure during actual need, including affected participant accounts and operating policy.
findings.falsify: Demonstrated access for intended users during the relevant event, with adequate alternate capacity.
findings.threshold: Rules or closure prevent intended participants obtaining essential service and alternatives cannot carry the load.
findings.uncertainty: No specific new law or pandemic closure is claimed in September 2026.

findings.claim: A commons may begin with modifiable space, seating/shade, light, water access, shared tools and relationships; formal ownership or a complete microgrid is not a prerequisite for usefulness. Additional rights, structures and energy can follow actual use.

This bounded thread did not verify a commissioned Oakland public resilience microgrid. A PG&E 2022 primary announcement is a strong lead for an operational North Coast counterexample to San Anselmo uniqueness; Ava currently advertises technical assistance and installation incentives. Neither establishes a particular Oakland hub is commissioned.
